title: ANDS Studio — Guided submission journey (home)
walkthrough:
The page opens with a top bar. On the left is the brand "ANDS Studio" with a small dot mark and the tagline "· guided ANDS filing". On the right sit a user chip and five navigation chips: "Help", "My dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry", and "Correspondence". Once a filing session exists, the top bar also shows a readiness chip — either "Ready to file" or a percentage like "62% ready" — and a "Reset session" button (clicking it opens a confirmation modal titled "Reset this session?" that requires typing RESET to confirm, explains it clears only the local session and does not delete your work, and notes the dossier and its append-only Part-11 audit trail remain recoverable).

Before a session starts, the page shows a hero. While a saved session is being checked, the screen reads "Loading your filing…". Otherwise the headline is "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." Below it, a paragraph: "An Abbreviated New Drug Submission is one of the most complex filings a company can make. This walks you through it step by step — every term explained in plain language with the regulatory vocabulary kept precise, the right pathway chosen for your product, and your submission's readiness visible at every moment until it's ready to send." The primary button reads "Start my submission →" (it shows "Starting…" and is disabled while working). Errors appear as a red notice with the error text. Below the button is a separated "Other ways to start" card holding two chip links — "Managing several products? Open the dossier catalog →" (with a count in parentheses when dossiers exist) and "Portfolio roll-up →" (with "· N in progress" when any are blocked) — and a note: "Labelling / regulatory: bilingual Module 1 and Product Monograph (EN + FR) status live inside each dossier — open a dossier's Module 1 to review it." Beneath that sits a Trust & security strip, and a quieter footnote reads "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

After starting, the layout becomes three columns. The left rail is titled "Your filing journey" and carries a mode toggle showing "Guided mode" (the default) or "Expert mode"; in Expert mode a line reads "Expert mode: later steps are navigable but marked not yet recommended — the guided order is still the safe path." The rail lists the steps. Each step shows a checkmark when done, a lock icon when locked, or its own icon; beneath each label is a status line — "Done", "You're here", the plain-language reason it is locked, or a regulatory reference. Completed and current steps are clickable to revisit; in Guided mode locked steps are not clickable and hovering shows the lock reason, while in Expert mode a locked step becomes navigable but is marked "⚠ Not yet recommended" with its reason.

The center is a step card headed by an eyebrow like "Step 3 of 10" plus a regulation reference, then the step's title and a purpose sentence. Step 1 ("orient") teaches: "You're about to file an ANDS — the pathway for a generic copy of an approved Canadian brand drug…" with underlined glossary terms (ANDS, bioequivalent, Canadian Reference Product). It contains the "Tell me about your drug" form: "I'll route you to the right pathway before you build anything." Fields: "What's your drug?" (placeholder "e.g. Drugazole 10 mg tablet"); "What are you filing?" with options "Generic of an approved brand (ANDS)", "A brand-new drug (NDS)", "Change to an existing generic (SANDS)", "Change to an existing brand (SNDS)", "DIN application"; "Dosage form" with "Immediate-release tablet/capsule", "Modified-release tablet/capsule", "Other / liquid / injectable"; and a checkbox "It's for a new use the brand isn't approved for". The "Check my pathway" button ("Checking…" while busy) returns a routing notice with a pathway label and advice, warning advisories prefixed "⚠", and — for an ANDS on the comparative-BE pathway — a note that Module 4 (nonclinical / animal studies) generally won't be needed.

Later steps follow the same pattern. The company step asks for "Your Health Canada Company ID" (placeholder "e.g. 12345") with an escape hatch: "I've requested it — flag as an open risk & continue →" (after which a persistent "⚠ Open risk tracked" notice explains you cannot transmit until the real 5-digit ID is set). The dossier step asks for a "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product type" (options: "Pharmaceutical / biologic", "Veterinary", "Medical device", "Master File (eCTD)"), validating the format on blur ("✓ Valid Dossier ID format." or an error). The submission step collects "Applicant (your company name)" and "Drug product". The content step links to "Open the Module builder →" with the hint "Build Modules 1–5 — upload or author every document with guidance"; its Continue button is disabled until the document gate is complete, showing "Place the required documents to continue" or a count like "3 required document(s) still needed across the modules." (and "✓ All required documents are in — you can continue." once complete). The validate step runs "full technical validation" and reports "✓ Validation passed — 12 document(s) checked, 0 warning(s)." or, on failure, "✗ N error(s) to fix", appending "(simulated)" when not run on real bytes. The fees step has a checkbox "My small-business status is already granted"; if it is unchecked, a warning appears: "⚠ Not granted yet? Apply for small-business status before filing or you forfeit the 50% reduction / first-submission waiver." Review, sign, and transmit steps show confirmations like "✓ QA review recorded", a signed e-signature manifest (signer, UTC time, meaning, reason, manifest hash, leaves signed, with a "Verify signature" button), and — behind a "Show the three receipts" expander with the summary "Transmission receipts: N of 3 received — you get three, in order (two FDA-side, then Health Canada's). Don't stop at the FDA ACK." — three receipt tiles: "FDA MDN", "FDA ACK", "HC ACK (Core ID)". The track step offers buttons to "Simulate a Health Canada notice to see the timers:" ("Log a screening deficiency (SDN)", "Log a clarifax (review question)", "Log a Notice of Deficiency (NOD)", "Log approval (NOC)"), countdown timers with "days left"/"days overdue", and a clarifax "Pause the clock"/"Resume the clock" toggle. Each step card ends with one primary button (e.g. "Continue →", showing "Working…" when busy) and a pointer like "Next: [next step name]".

The right column shows the "Submission tower" — a 3D stack (or a CSS fallback), with a "3D view" / "Checklist" toggle, captioned "Your submission · Module 1–5 — 4/10 green" (appending "· READY ✦" when ready), switching during the content step to "Placing into Module 1–5 — 2/4 complete". Below it, the "Readiness" card shows "● READY TO FILE" or "● BLOCKED", a line like "Filing checklist: 6 of 10 steps complete (60%)", a separate "eCTD technical validation" verdict line (either "not yet run", "passed — 0 errors across N checks", or an error count) noted as structural checks against a named validator profile and "not HC's official eValidator", a progress bar, step tiles, and — when blocked — "The single thing standing between you and ready:" with the blocker and a resume button. When ready: "Everything checks out — your package is ready to transmit to Health Canada."
